title: Plane wave on a perfectly conducting sphere (radius 5 mm, ka = 1.05) at 10 GHz: scattering and radar cross-sections
source: The Mie series of a perfectly conducting sphere, aₙ = ψₙ'(ka)/ξₙ'(ka), bₙ = ψₙ(ka)/ξₙ(ka) (J. A. Stratton, Electromagnetic Theory, 1941, §9.25; C. F. Bohren, D. R. Huffman, 1983, §4.4); the back-scatter σ/πa² = 3.65 near ka = 1 is the classic peak of the sphere's monostatic RCS (Bowman, Senior, Uslenghi, Electromagnetic and Acoustic Scattering by Simple Shapes, 1969, §10.3)

quantities.reason: the scattered field on the curved sphere set to −n × E_inc by L² projection, six second-order elements per wavelength, a 12 mm layer: +0.5 %
